data.description:
# Respawn player in same spot

## Original request (verbatim seed)

> When a player is hit show they should respawn in the same spot. The routine should be: 1) Play SFX
> 2) Play VFX (expand the ship by 50% then contract to normal size) 3) respawn ship in current
> location and orientation (with existing invincibility time out)

## Problem statement

When the player ship is hit in a gym scene it is currently **relocated to a fixed spawn point**
(centre screen) rather than staying where it was hit. The operator wants a hit to read as a short
"damage beat" at the point of impact: play the existing SFX, play a scale VFX (ship grows to 150%
then shrinks back to 100%) **in addition to** the existing particle burst, then leave the ship
**stopped dead at the same position and orientation** it had when hit, under the existing post-hit
invulnerability window.

Initial spawn is **not** changing: a new game / scene start still spawns the ship centre screen.

## Users

- **Players** — a hit should look and feel like a damage flash on the ship they are flying, not a
  teleport back to the middle of the screen that loses their position in the level.
- **Designers / AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need one unambiguous, testable rule for
  "respawn in place" so all player-bearing scenes behave identically.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship to stay where it was hit so I keep my position and the hit reads
  as a damage effect rather than a relocation.
- As a **player**, I want a clear visual beat (ship pulses to 150% and back to normal) layered on the
  existing explosion so the hit is unmistakable, plus the existing hit sound.
- As a **developer**, I want the in-place respawn implemented once in the shared player-hit path so
  every gym scene inherits identical behaviour and tests stay cheap.
- As a **developer**, I want the start-of-scene spawn position to remain unchanged, so this change
  cannot silently regress "player spawns centre screen".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-place respawn after death:** After a player hit, the ship occupies the **same (x, y)**
  it had at the moment of the hit; it is not relocated to the scene's fixed spawn point
  (`playerSpawnX/Y`, `PLAYER_SPAWN`, or centre screen).
- [ ] **AC2 — Spawn (new game / scene start) unchanged:** The initial spawn position is **not** changed
  — the ship still spawns centre screen (`PLAYER_SPAWN` / scene config) on scene start. Only the
  post-hit respawn is in-place.
- [ ] **AC3 — State on respawn:** The ship's **facing/orientation at the moment of the hit is
  preserved** (the respawn must not reset rotation to 0 / facing to a default) and its
  **velocity/momentum is reset to zero** — the ship is **stopped dead** at the hit spot.
- [ ] **AC4 — Hit VFX (scale pulse):** The hit plays a visible scale VFX on the ship: scale **expands
  to ~150%** of normal and then **contracts back to 100%**, ending at exactly 1.0 scale. The VFX is
  observable from tests (or deterministically assertable) without pixel comparison.
- [ ] **AC5 — Hit VFX is additive:** The scale pulse plays **in addition to** the existing
  particle-explosion burst (`_spawnPlayerExplosion` / shared particle helper). Entity death VFX is
  unchanged.
- [ ] **AC6 — Hit SFX and invulnerability unchanged:** The existing hit/destruction SFX still plays
  exactly once per hit (no double-play, no new audio asset), and the post-hit invulnerability window
  and blink keep their existing per-scene values (`PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE` = 1.5 s in
  `GymFormationScene`; `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION` = 0.8 s in `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC7 — Scope consistent:** The in-place respawn + scale VFX applies to **every player-hit path**
  — `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (inherited by `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, and the formation gyms) and
  `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` — so no scene keeps the old relocate-to-spawn behaviour.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** Unit/scene tests cover: (a) post-hit position equals pre-hit
  position; (b) pre-hit facing is preserved exactly (a silent reset-to-0 must fail); (c) velocity is
  zero after the hit; (d) the scale pulse runs 1.0 → 1.5 → 1.0; (e) the particle burst still spawns
  (additive VFX); (f) SFX fires once; (g) invulnerability is set and a second hit is ignored while it
  is active; (h) initial spawn position is unchanged. All tests pass.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.2 ("Collisions &
  respawn") is updated from "the ship respawns at its spawn position" to the in-place rule, noting
  that the *respawn* clause of AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC4 is superseded while its *initial spawn* rule
  stands. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Initial spawn must not change** — centre-screen spawn (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC1–AC3) remains in
  force; only the post-hit respawn rule is superseded.
- **No new audio asset** — reuse the existing destruction SFX (`playDestructionSound`).
- **No change to lives/score model** — the player is never destroyed (infinite lives in gyms); only
  the respawn location/orientation/velocity and the hit VFX change.
- **No change to the collision radii or hit conditions** that trigger `_hitPlayer()`.
- **Deterministic tests preferred** — Phaser tweens are awkward to assert; expose an observable seam
  (e.g. a tracked scale-VFX handle or a `getPlayerHitVfx()` accessor) rather than relying on
  wall-clock tween completion.
- **Merge-order awareness** — `GymFormationScene.ts` is a shared core library touched by many gym
  items; keep the diff surgical.

## Existing state

- `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, ~line 834):
  increments `playerHitCount`, calls `playDestructionSound()`, calls
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion(player.x, player.y)` (particle burst, `SHIP_COLOR`/`SHIP_SIZE`), then
  `this.player.respawn(this.playerSpawnX, this.playerSpawnY)` and sets
  `playerInvulnerable = PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE` (1.5 s) with blink reset.
- `playerSpawnX/Y` are captured at `create()` from `config.player.x/y` (centre screen,
  `PLAYER_SPAWN = { x: 480, y: 270 }` per AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT).
- `Player.respawn(x, y)` (`src/entities/Player.ts`, ~line 800) **hard-resets** the movement state to
  `{ x, y, vx: 0, vy: 0, facing: 0 }`, calls `setRotation(0)`, zeroes thruster flames and stops the
  thruster hum — i.e. it zeroes velocity (which we want) but **also discards orientation** (which we
  must preserve).
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, ~line 657) independently
  hard-codes a relocate to `GAME_WIDTH/2, GAME_HEIGHT/2`, zeroes velocity, plays
  `playDestructionSound()`, and starts invulnerability = `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION` (0.8 s).
  It has **no** particle or scale VFX.
- Particle burst VFX for player death was introduced by "Wire particle VFX to death paths"
  (AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J) as the **primary** death VFX for both entities and the player; it stays.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.2 ("Collisions & respawn", ~lines 406–417) documents
  the current relocate-to-spawn behaviour; ~line 416 states "the ship respawns at its spawn
  position".
- Superseded in part: "Player should spawn center screen" (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT) AC4 required "the
  respawn position matches the initial spawn position (center screen)" — its respawn clause is
  superseded by this item; its initial-spawn clauses remain valid.

## Desired change

On a player hit, run exactly this sequence at the ship's current position:

1. **SFX** — play the existing destruction sound once.
2. **VFX** — scale the ship up to ~150% and back down to 100% (a single expand/contract pulse),
   **in addition to** the existing particle-explosion burst.
3. **Respawn** — leave the ship at its **current location and current orientation**, with
   **velocity zeroed (stopped dead)**, and start the **existing** post-hit invulnerability window
   (blink).

No relocation to the fixed spawn point, and no orientation reset. The initial spawn position on
scene start is unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` becomes in-place; add the scale-VFX
  pulse (and an observable seam); keep SFX, particle burst and `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE`.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `respawn()` needs a variant/mode that preserves orientation (currently
  forces `facing: 0` / `setRotation(0)`); velocity-zeroing behaviour is retained or a new
  `respawnInPlace()` is added.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` must adopt the same in-place + scale VFX +
  SFX behaviour (currently hard-codes centre-screen relocation and has no VFX).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5) / pulse-duration constant.
  `PLAYER_SPAWN` must remain `{ x: 480, y: 270 }`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — update/extend tests for position, orientation, velocity, scale
  pulse, particle burst, SFX, invulnerability and unchanged initial spawn.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §7.2 collisions/respawn wording.

## Related work

- **Player should spawn center screen (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT)** — **partially superseded**: its AC4
  respawn clause ("respawn position matches the initial spawn position") is replaced by the in-place
  rule; its AC1–AC3 initial-spawn rule (centre screen on scene start) remains in force and is
  guarded by AC2 here.
- **Wire particle VFX to death paths (AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J)** — introduced the particle burst as the
  *primary* player-death VFX (`_spawnPlayerExplosion`). Operator decision: the new scale pulse is
  **additive** to it (AC5).
- **Implement: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH)** —
  created the original hit → SFX + explosion + respawn-at-spawn + invulnerability path.
- **Test: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB)** — existing
  hit/respawn test coverage that will need updating.
- **If player crashes into an enemy, they both die (AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT)** — the entity-collision
  branch also calls `_hitPlayer()`; it inherits the in-place rule decided here.
- **Implement/Test: Wipe detection, 3s countdown, and respawn in GymFormationScene
  (AH-0MTHCD0BQ000JFZ4 / AH-0MTHCFDAD009B3JG)** — the *formation* respawn lifecycle (unrelated
  mechanism, same file and same `respawn` vocabulary — do not conflate).
- **Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library (AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3)** — why the player-hit
  logic lives in one shared base class.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Resolved — reversing a producer-approved AC (partial):** AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC4 is superseded
  **for respawn only**, by explicit operator decision (Appendix Q1). Its initial-spawn rule stands;
  AC2 is the regression guard. Note the supersede in the §7.2 documentation update (AC9).
- **Resolved — VFX relationship:** the scale pulse plays **in addition to** the particle burst
  (Appendix Q3); entity death VFX unchanged.
- **Resolved — velocity:** zeroed on respawn — "stopped dead" (Appendix Q2).
- **Risk — orientation is not currently recoverable after `respawn()`:** `Player.respawn()` discards
  `facing`; the implementer must capture position/orientation **before** calling any reset, or add an
  in-place variant. Tests must assert the exact pre-hit facing (not merely "unchanged"), so a silent
  reset-to-0 cannot pass (AC8b).
- **Risk — two independent hit paths:** `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` does not extend
  `GymFormationScene` and currently has neither particle nor scale VFX; it must be brought in line
  or the scope AC (AC7) fails. Consider extracting the hit beat into a shared helper to avoid a third
  divergence.
- **Risk — tween test flakiness:** scale tweens are time-based; expose a deterministic seam (AC4) or
  drive the pulse from `tick(dt)` as the countdown is, to keep the suite stable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** keep the change to the hit/respawn beat only. Extra ideas surfaced while
  planning (e.g. brief slow-motion on hit, hit-screen shake, per-scene VFX variation, hit-count UI)
  must be recorded as **linked new work items**, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** "expand the ship by 50%" means peak scale 1.5× of the ship's normal scale, returning
  to exactly 1.0.
- **Assumption:** `GymPlayer` has no hit logic, so it is out of scope unless the operator says
  otherwise.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Respawn in place **supersedes** AC4 of *Player should spawn center screen*
  (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT), which required respawn to relocate to the centre-screen spawn point. Should
  the in-place rule replace the relocate-to-spawn rule in **all** player-hit scenes
  (GymFormationScene base → GymEnemies / GymBoss / formation gyms, plus GymPowerUpsCombat)?
  [Proposed: yes — respawn in place everywhere, old AC4 superseded.]" — **Answer (operator): "When
  starting a new game, spawn central. When re-spawning after death supersede."** Source: interactive
  reply. Interpretation (accepted): the **initial spawn stays centre screen**; the **respawn**
  behaviour is superseded to in-place across all player-hit scenes. Final: AC1 (in-place respawn) +
  AC2 (initial spawn unchanged) + AC7 (all hit paths).
- Q2: "At the moment of a hit, should the ship **keep its pre-hit velocity/momentum** (so it carries
  on drifting after the VFX), or be **stopped dead** at the hit spot while preserving position and
  facing? [Proposed: stopped dead — position + orientation preserved, velocity zeroed, matching the
  existing `respawn()` behaviour for velocity.]" — **Answer (operator): "stop dead"**. Source:
  interactive reply. Final: AC3 — orientation preserved, velocity zeroed.
- Q3: "Does the expand-to-150%-then-contract scale VFX **replace** the existing particle-explosion
  burst on player hit (`_spawnPlayerExplosion`, added as the *primary* death VFX by
  AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J), or **play in addition to** it? [Proposed: replace for the player hit (one
  clear damage beat); keep entities' particle bursts unchanged.]" — **Answer (operator): "in
  addition"**. Source: interactive reply. Final: AC5 — scale pulse is additive to the particle
  burst; entity death VFX unchanged.
- Research note: the player-hit path was read directly at `GymFormationScene.ts:697–843`,
  `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts:657–675` and `Player.ts:800`. The centre-screen spawn rule and its AC4
  wording were read from AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT; the particle-burst-as-primary-VFX decision from
  AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J AC1–AC3. Invulnerability constants: `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5` and
  `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8` in `src/core/constants.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5** – Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules in GDD (Wall vs Dive Bomb) (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBY430008GB2** – Diver should always turn to face the player (completed)
- **AH-0MTAN4T0I004H187** – Rewrite GymTank gym scene on the core library (completed)
